messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
tiel mia animo, kiu ankoraŭ flugis, turniĝis reen por rigardi la pason kiu neniam forlasis vivantan personon.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | così | resultative adverb “so” | tiel | “so / thus” | OK | | l'animo | “the soul” (subject) | animo | “soul” | UNNECESSARY (article “l’” dropped – Esperanto has no definite article) | | mio | possessive adjective “my” | mia | “my” | OK | | ch'ancor | relative pronoun “which” + adverb “still” | kiu ankoraŭ | “which still” | OK | | fuggiva | imperfect “was fleeing / flying” | flugis | “flew / was flying” | OK | | si | reflexive clitic (the soul turns **itself**) | – (reflexivity encoded in *turniĝis*) | – | UNNECESSARY | | volse | past “turned” (reflexive) | turniĝis | “turned (reflexively)” | OK | | a (1) | preposition introducing direction “to” (part of *a retro*) | – (merged into *reen*) | – | UNNECESSARY | | retro | noun used adverbially “back” | reen | “backward” | OK | | a (2) | preposition introducing purpose “to” (before infinitive) | por | “for / in order to” | OK | | rimirar | infinitive “to look again” | rigardi | “to look / to gaze” | OK | | lo | definite article “the” (masc.) | la | “the” | OK | | passo | “the pass” (object) | pason | “the pass” (accusative) | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which” | kiu | “which” | OK | | non | negation particle “not” | neniam | “never” (combined with *mai*) | OK | | lasciò | past “left” | forlasis | “left / abandoned” | OK | | già | temporal adverb “already” | – (omitted) | – | **MISSING** | | mai | adverb “never” (intensifier) | neniam | “never” (covers both *non* + *mai*) | OK | | persona | noun “person” | personon | “person” (accusative) | OK | | viva | adjective “living” (agreeing with *persona*) | vivantan | “living” (accusative) | OK |
### Items to Address - **MISSING:** *già* (“already”) – not rendered in the Esperanto line; the translation could add *jam* or *jam antaŭe* if the nuance is required. - **UNNECESSARY:** *l’* (definite article), *si* (reflexive clitic), first *a* (directional preposition) – Esperanto does not need these elements; their meaning is conveyed by other words or morphology. - **GRAMMAR:** None detected; all retained words agree in case, number, and gender.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Esperanto script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Esperanto text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
